questions.q: A feature opens with three lovely paragraphs about a beekeeper, then moves on to statistics about colony collapse with no transition. What's missing?
choices: A kicker
A summary lede
A nut graf that says what the story is about and why it matters now
A point of insight
questions.explain: The nut graf connects the anecdote to the larger subject and makes the promise the rest of the story keeps.

questions.q: Put the feature formula in order.
choices: Nut graf, anecdotal lede, kicker, body
Anecdotal lede, nut graf, body, kicker
Anecdotal lede, body, nut graf, kicker
Summary lede, body, nut graf, kicker
questions.explain: Anecdote first to draw readers in, the nut graf to say why, the body for evidence, and a kicker to end.

questions.q: Why must the lede anecdote be representative as well as vivid?
choices: Otherwise it may mislead readers about the larger subject
Because editors cut it first
Because it must contain all five Ws
Because the kicker must quote the same person
questions.explain: An extreme case presented as typical can exaggerate a trend or misdescribe it.

questions.q: Blundell argued that most bad features fail where?
choices: In the kicker
In copy editing
In the choice of headline
Before the writing: in the reporting and thinking
questions.explain: He offered dimensions to report, such as history, scope, reasons, impact, countermoves and future, so writers know what the story is.

questions.q: A reporter is covering a housing trend that is still unfolding, with no resolution in sight. Which structure fits best?
choices: Franklin's complication-and-resolution outline, which needs a real ending
A five-act tragedy
The feature formula, whose question is 'what's going on here?'
None: stories without endings shouldn't be written
questions.explain: The feature formula doesn't need a resolution, which makes it useful exactly when a narrative can't be told.

choices: Restates the nut graf word for word
Returns to the person from the opening, seen in light of everything learned
Summarizes the five Ws
Introduces a new character for the next story
questions.explain: Returning to the lede's person gives a sense of closure and lets the reader see them anew.

questions.q: What's a common criticism of the formula today?
choices: The reflexive 'Jane Doe, 47' lede has become a cliché, and the anecdote can personalize a structural problem
It's too short for newspapers
It gives away the ending in the first line
It forbids statistics
questions.explain: Readers recognize the formula, and a single human case can misrepresent a systemic issue.

ideas: Open with one person in a vivid moment, then pull back to say why that moment stands for something bigger.
Move from the specific to the general and back again, ending where you began.
Before writing about a trend, report its history, scope, causes, impact, countermoves and future.
